clue.text: Nothing interrupts torchlit military band

annotationWithheld.why: Nothing interrupts torchlit military band (6): the only parse is O + an anagram of TORCH, so the single printed word 'torchlit' is both fodder (torch) and anagram indicator (lit)

clue.text: Audible mistake made by bell-ringers?

definitions.note: the definition describes a noise rather than naming it: the din that bell-ringers produce

indicators.note: audible means heard rather than seen, so the word for a mistake is to be taken as it sounds

parts.note: a clanger is a British colloquial word for a blunder

explanation.surface: A bell-ringing team drops a howler that the whole parish can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audible' signals a word that sounds like another: a CLANGER (British slang for a blunder) said aloud is near enough to the word for a loud ringing din.
explanation.definitionFit: Clangour is a loud resonant ringing, exactly the racket a team of bell-ringers produces.

clue.text: Control mechanism restraining Germany with difficulty

indicators.note: restraining means holding something in, so the harness holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a harness is gear for controlling a horse or a person
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Some device struggles to keep Germany in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restraining' puts D (Germany) inside HARNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardness can mean difficulty, as in the hardness of a task or problem.

clue.text: Soldiers turned to God in Latin 5

definitions.note: the cross-reference stands for the answer to 5 down, entertainment

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the letters for soldiers are read the other way

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
deo is Latin for 'to God', as in Deo gratias

explanation.surface: Troops come round to praising the Lord in a Latin show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes RO from OR (other ranks); the 5 refers to 5 down, ENTERTAINMENT, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a public show of riding skills, a form of entertainment.

clue.text: Initially regular sorties disrupted by electrical component

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of regular is taken
disrupted means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Routine raids thrown off course by a faulty electrical part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' gives R from regular; 'disrupted' rearranges SORTIES into ESISTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A resistor is a basic component in an electrical circuit that limits current flow.

clue.text: Infiltrate marquee housing travesty of main turn

parts.note: to infiltrate a place is to enter it

indicators.note: housing means holding within, so the tent wraps round the scrambled letters

parts.note: a marquee is a large tent

indicators.note: a travesty is a grotesque distortion, so the next word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gatecrash the big tent, which holds a mockery of the main act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' at the end looks like an instruction, but it is the definition: a performer's act. 'travesty of' scrambles the fodder that 'housing' tucks into the marquee.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn is a performer's act on stage, a piece of entertainment.

clue.text: Sickness calling for medication — not initially on toast

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is dropped from the word for medication

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medication
'Your health!' is a toast drunk to someone

explanation.surface: Someone is too poorly for the celebratory toast and needs a pill instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' drops the first letter of the medication; 'calling for' just links. A toast is drunk 'Your health!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill health is a state of sickness, the kind that needs treating with medicine.

clue.text: Fools about with famous Belgian?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the fools are read backwards

parts.note: a nit is a British informal word for a fool; two of them for the plural

explanation.surface: Idiots messing around with a celebrated man from Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns NITNIT (two nits, British slang for fools) round. Tintin is the boy reporter of Hergé's comics, perhaps the best-known Belgian of all, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintin, Hergé's comic-book reporter, is often joked to be the most famous Belgian.

clue.text: Make allusion about drug joint

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for alluding goes round the drug

parts.note: to make allusion to something is to refer to it
E is the abbreviation for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Hinting at drugs when talking about a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drug joint' reads as one phrase, but the drug is E (ecstasy) and 'joint' alone is the definition; 'about' puts REFER round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a slang term for a cannabis cigarette, also called a joint.

clue.text: It's biting cold and dry outside

indicators.note: outside means the dry word sits round the cold letter

parts.note: arid means dry
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A remark about the weather: it is bitterly cold and dry out there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' places ARID around C (cold); 'biting' is not about the weather but the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid describes a sharp, pungent taste or smell, one that is biting.

clue.text: Moodiness of sweetheart taking turn with weapon

parts.note: pet is a term of endearment, like sweetheart
a U-turn is a turn, so U stands for one
a lance is a long spear-like weapon

explanation.surface: A lover turns sulky and picks up a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: U stands for a turn, from the U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is childish sulkiness or bad temper, a kind of moodiness.

clue.text: Screws leader of Polish cavalry carrying offspring to battle

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of Polish is taken
carrying means bearing within, so the horsemen enclose the next pieces

parts.note: cavalry are soldiers on horseback, riders
a son is offspring
war is battle

explanation.surface: Cavalry led by a Polish commander take a child off to war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screws' looks like a verb, but it is British prison slang for warders; 'leader of' takes the first letter and 'carrying' puts offspring and battle inside the horsemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Screws is British slang for prison officers, the people who guard inmates.

clue.text: Boatman, one doomed to ship broken idol

indicators.note: to ship means to take aboard, so the doomed one holds the next letters

parts.note: a goner is someone doomed or past saving

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boatman, already doomed, has to carry aboard a shattered statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns IDOL into DOLI, and 'to ship' takes it aboard GONER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondolier is the boatman who rows a gondola in Venice.

clue.text: Cut short from midfield to cover point

parts.note: the centre letter of the word field, taken from its middle
a lid is a cover
E is a point of the compass, east

explanation.surface: A footballer pulls up from the middle of the pitch to guard a spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from midfield' gives E, the middle letter of 'field'; then LID (cover) and E, a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To elide is to cut short a word by slurring or omitting a sound or syllable.

clue.text: Badly timed and impervious to salt?

definitions.meaning: out of keeping with the time of year, or ill-timed
jokingly, something that cannot take salt as flavouring

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: seasoning is salt and pepper, so a thing that will not take salt cannot be seasoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Unseasonable means ill-timed, and read literally it means incapable of being given seasoning.

clue.text: A vapour getting into the food in Farewell to Arms

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so the vapour goes inside the food

parts.note: rice is a staple food
mist is fine water vapour

explanation.surface: Steam rising off a dish in a scene from Hemingway's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Farewell to Arms' recalls Hemingway's novel, but read literally it means laying down weapons; 'getting into' puts the vapour inside the food.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a truce when fighting stops, literally a farewell to weapons.

clue.text: Highly desirable female smell, rising, captivates virtuous man

indicators.note: captivates means holds captive, so the saint is held within
rising in a down entry means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Eva is a female name
hum is British slang for a bad smell
ST, saint, is a virtuous man

explanation.surface: A woman's scent wafts up and charms a good man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reads the woman and the smell upwards (MUHAVE) and 'captivates' holds the saint inside. Hum is British slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: A must-have is something so desirable people feel they cannot do without it.

clue.text: Portray second copy in flower

indicators.note: in means the pieces are placed inside the river

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, here the River Dee
to crib is to copy

explanation.surface: Depict a second reproduction of a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is not a bloom but a river, something that flows: the Dee. 'in' puts S + CRIB inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To describe something is to portray it in words.

clue.text: Singer having a drink chez moi?

parts.note: chez moi is French for 'at my place', so moi gives the possessive 'my'
wine is a drink
chez means at the house of

explanation.surface: Someone invites a famous vocalist round for a glass at their place.
explanation.walkthrough: Chez moi is French for 'at my place', so a drink chez moi is a my wine house. Amy Winehouse was a British soul singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amy Winehouse was a celebrated British soul and jazz singer.

clue.text: Shakespearean sea creature concealing identity, after reflection

indicators.note: after reflection means as seen in a mirror, so the whole is read backwards
concealing means hiding within, so the creature holds the identity letters

parts.note: a crab is a sea creature
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: A creature of the sea in a Shakespeare play hides its true self, then reconsiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' gives CIDRAB, which 'after reflection' reads backwards, as in a mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare is known as the Bard, so bardic can mean Shakespearean.

clue.text: Ne plus ultra concerning Paris?

parts.note: ne plus ultra is the utmost limit; to the hilt means to the utmost
on means concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A question about the ultimate in Parisian style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' looks like the city, but it is Paris Hilton, the American celebrity heiress, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilton is the surname of Paris Hilton, the celebrity heiress, so it fits her first name.

clue.text: Heretic's study of Scriptures down under

annotationWithheld.why: Heretic's study of Scriptures down under (5): RI inside AUS, but 'down under' must both give AUS and signal the insertion, one phrase doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Heretic's study of Scriptures down under

clue.text: Creaky chair mute after treatment

indicators.note: after treatment means once worked on and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old chair makes no noise once it has been repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creaky' sounds like the chair, but it is the definition, describing stiff joints; 'after treatment' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatic describes stiff aching joints, the way a creaky old person moves.

clue.text: Model absorbing energy from Jewish leader

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the model takes in the energy letter

parts.note: Kate Moss is a famous British model
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A fashion model soaks up vitality from a Jewish leader.
explanation.walkthrough: MOSS is Kate Moss, the British supermodel; 'absorbing' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt and is a central Jewish leader.

clue.text: Deleterious effect of thaw almost drowning border

indicators.note: drowning means submerging, so the shortened thaw covers the border
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: detente is a thaw in relations between countries
a rim is a border

explanation.surface: A thaw nearly floods the borderland, doing damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thaw' is a political easing between nations, not melting ice; 'almost' drops its last letter to give DETENT, and 'drowning' sinks the border inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment means harm or damage, a deleterious effect.

clue.text: Teacher travelled by water to Italy

parts.note: swam means travelled through water
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An instructor swims all the way to Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher or holy man.

clue.text: Scam to get back valuable item from European aristocrat

parts.note: a con is a scam

indicators.note: to get back means going in reverse, so the valuable item is read backwards

parts.note: an asset is something of value

explanation.surface: A swindle to recover a treasure from a continental noblewoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get back' reads the valuable item backwards (TESSA) after the scam.
explanation.definitionFit: A contessa is an Italian countess, a European noblewoman.

clue.text: Ascetic East German city, formerly

indicators.note: formerly means before, so the city comes ahead of the compass letter

parts.note: Essen is a city in western Germany

explanation.surface: A hermit from a city in the old East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' looks like the old GDR, but East is just E; 'formerly' places ESSEN before it. The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ancient Jewish sect known for strict self-denial, so one is an ascetic.
